en.greeting: Hi! Today we go deeper into small words with a big job: no article or the, and quantifiers like each, every, both, either, neither and none. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: General meaning: no article
steps.text: You know a/an and the. At B2 the hard part is knowing when English uses no article at all.
steps.body:
Talking **in general** (all of it, the idea) about an **uncountable** noun (*life, music, money*) or a **plural** noun (*children, doctors*)? Use **no article**: *Life is hard. Children need love. I love music.*

The trap: *Hidup **itu** berat* makes people say `The life is hard`. Here *itu* only marks the topic; it isn't *the*.

And English must choose: *Saya suka kucing* = I like **cats** (plural), not `I like cat`.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi is writing an essay for his IELTS class. He means technology in general.

question.prompt: Complete the first sentence of his essay: ___ makes our lives easier.
question.explanation: Technology **in general** is uncountable, so **no article**: *Technology makes our lives easier.* `The technology` would mean one particular technology you both know, and *a* can't go with an uncountable noun.

steps.title: the: this one, or the only one
steps.text: Now the other side: when does the same word need the?
steps.body:
A noun becomes **specific** when you both know **which one**. Words like **of …**, **in/at …** or **that …** often point to it: *History is my favourite subject* → ***The** history of Jakarta is interesting.* *I love music* → *I don't like **the** music in this café.*

Also **the** for things there's **only one of**: *the sun, the internet, the government, the police*.

At B2 this is a strong tendency: *Life in Jakarta is busy* is still general. Ask: do I mean **this particular** one?

steps.title: Places: school or the school?
steps.text: Places have a short list of their own.
steps.body:
Go somewhere **for its main purpose** (study, work, sleep, pray in church)? **No article**: *go to school, go to work, go to bed, be at home.* Go to the **building** for another reason? **the**: *go to the school for a meeting.* Most other places always take the: *the office, the bank, the station, the mosque.*

**British vs American:** *in hospital* (British, a patient) = *in the hospital* (American). Both are correct.

examples.en: My daughter goes to school by ojek.
examples.id: Anak perempuan saya berangkat sekolah naik ojek.

examples.en: Bu Ani went to the school to talk to her son's teacher.
examples.id: Bu Ani pergi ke sekolah untuk bicara dengan guru anaknya.

examples.en: Rina goes to the office three days a week.
examples.id: Rina ke kantor tiga hari seminggu.
Kakek saya dirawat di rumah sakit. (British)

examples.en: My grandfather is in the hospital.
examples.id: Kakek saya dirawat di rumah sakit. (Amerika)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari has a new job at an NGO in Bandung. She explains what it does.

question.prompt: Complete: Our organisation works to protect ___.
question.explanation: **the environment** = the natural world around us. There's only one, so **the**, like *the internet* and *the government*. With no article it sounds wrong, and *an environment* would be one of many (like *a work environment*).

steps.title: each and every
steps.text: Now quantifiers: words that say how many. First, each and every.
steps.body:
Both mean *setiap* and take a **singular** noun and verb: *Every student **has** a laptop.* Not `every students`: think *every **one** student*.
- **every** = all of a group (three or more): *Every seat was taken.*
- **each** = one by one, separately; also for **two**: *each side of the road*.
- Before **of**, only each: *each of the rooms*. Not `every of` (say *every one of*).

Looks like a broken rule: *every two weeks*. The two weeks are one period that repeats.

pairs.id: setiap rekan kerja saya (satu per satu)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Hasan runs a training course for new bank staff.

question.prompt: Complete: ___ of the trainees gets a certificate at the end of the course.
question.explanation: Before **of**, use **each**: *Each of the trainees gets …* with a singular verb (**gets**). `Every of` is wrong: you'd need *every one of*. *All of the trainees* would need a plural verb: *get*.

steps.title: both, either, neither, none
steps.text: Next: words for two things, and one for three or more.
steps.body:
For **two**:
- **both** = keduanya: *Both of my parents work.* (plural)
- **either** = salah satu, yang mana saja: *You can take either bus.*
- **neither** = tidak dua-duanya: *Neither answer is right.*
For **three or more** (or uncountable): **none of**: *None of my colleagues drives.*

**neither** and **none** are already negative: `Neither of them didn't come` ✗.

After *none of / neither of* + plural, a singular or plural verb is fine. And: *most people* (general), *most of my friends* (specific).

pairs.id: tidak satu pun dari dua jawaban
tidak satu pun rekan kerja saya
tidak sepeser pun dari uang itu

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina and her husband are invited to a colleague's dinner, but they're both busy that night.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kami berdua tidak bisa datang ke acara makan malam itu.
question.solution: Neither of us can come to the dinner.
question.explanation: **Neither of us** = kami berdua tidak. *neither* is already negative, so the verb stays positive: **can come**, not *can't come*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas needs cash for an ojek, so he looks for an ATM near the station.

question.prompt: Complete: He tried three ATMs, but ___ of them had any cash.
question.explanation: Three ATMs is more than two, so **none of**. *neither* is only for two, and *both* is for two and positive, so it doesn't fit with *but … any*.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is the whole lesson on one page.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · articles and quantifiers
artifact.intro: General = no article. Specific or only one = the. each/every + singular. both, either, neither for two; none for three or more.
rows: Life is hard. I love music.
Hidup itu berat. Saya suka musik.
the sun, the internet, the government
no article: main purpose of the place
go to school, go to work, go to bed
go to the school for a meeting
Kakek saya dirawat di rumah sakit.
each (one by one; also for two)
each side of the road, each of the rooms
Kamu bisa naik bus yang mana saja.
Tidak satu pun rekan kerja saya menyetir.
most / all / some of + the/my + noun
Most of my friends live in Bekasi.
Kebanyakan teman saya tinggal di Bekasi.
tips: General = no article: `The life is hard` → **Life is hard**. *itu* in *Hidup itu berat* isn't *the*.
**every** + singular: not `every students`. Two things or before **of** → **each**.
**neither** and **none** are already negative: `Neither … didn't` → **Neither of them came**. General: **most people**, not `most of people`.

examples.en: I love music, but I don't like the music in this café.
examples.id: Saya suka musik, tapi saya tidak suka musik di kafe ini.

examples.en: Bu Ani went to the school to talk to her son's teacher.
examples.id: Bu Ani pergi ke sekolah untuk bicara dengan guru anaknya.

examples.en: There are shops on each side of the road.
examples.id: Ada toko di kedua sisi jalan.

examples.en: None of the trains are running because of the flood.
examples.id: Tidak ada kereta yang jalan karena banjir.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more? These two British Council reference pages explain the and quantifiers like each, every, both, either and neither, with short exercises.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita mendalami kata-kata kecil dengan tugas besar: tanpa artikel atau the, dan quantifier seperti each, every, both, either, neither dan none. Ayo kita mulai pelan-pelan.

steps.title: Makna umum: tanpa artikel
steps.text: Kamu sudah tahu a/an dan the. Di level B2, bagian sulitnya adalah tahu kapan bahasa Inggris tidak memakai artikel sama sekali.
steps.body:
Membicarakan sesuatu **secara umum** (semuanya, idenya) dengan kata benda **tak terhitung** (*life, music, money*) atau kata benda **jamak** (*children, doctors*)? **Jangan pakai artikel**: *Life is hard. Children need love. I love music.*

Jebakannya: *Hidup **itu** berat* membuat orang bilang `The life is hard`. Di sini *itu* hanya menandai topiknya; itu bukan *the*.

Dan bahasa Inggris harus memilih: *Saya suka kucing* = I like **cats** (jamak), bukan `I like cat`.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi sedang menulis esai untuk kelas IELTS-nya. Maksudnya teknologi secara umum.

question.prompt: Lengkapi kalimat pertama esainya: ___ makes our lives easier.
question.explanation: Teknologi **secara umum** itu tak terhitung, jadi **tanpa artikel**: *Technology makes our lives easier.* `The technology` berarti satu teknologi tertentu yang kalian sama-sama tahu, dan *a* tidak bisa dipakai dengan kata benda tak terhitung.

steps.title: the: yang ini, atau yang hanya satu
steps.text: Sekarang sisi lainnya: kapan kata yang sama butuh the?
steps.body:
Kata benda jadi **spesifik** kalau kalian sama-sama tahu **yang mana**. Kata seperti **of …**, **in/at …** atau **that …** sering menunjuknya: *History is my favourite subject* → ***The** history of Jakarta is interesting.* *I love music* → *I don't like **the** music in this café.*

Pakai **the** juga untuk benda yang **hanya ada satu**: *the sun, the internet, the government, the police*.

Di B2 ini kecenderungan kuat: *Life in Jakarta is busy* tetap umum. Tanya dirimu: apakah maksudku **yang tertentu ini**?

steps.title: Tempat: school atau the school?
steps.text: Tempat punya daftar pendeknya sendiri.
steps.body:
Pergi ke suatu tempat **untuk tujuan utamanya** (belajar, kerja, tidur, ibadah di gereja)? **Tanpa artikel**: *go to school, go to work, go to bed, be at home.* Ke **gedungnya** untuk urusan lain? **the**: *go to the school for a meeting.* Kebanyakan tempat lain selalu pakai the: *the office, the bank, the station, the mosque.*

**British vs Amerika:** *in hospital* (British, pasien) = *in the hospital* (Amerika). Keduanya benar.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sari punya pekerjaan baru di sebuah LSM di Bandung. Dia menjelaskan apa kerja lembaganya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Our organisation works to protect ___.
question.explanation: **the environment** = lingkungan hidup, alam di sekitar kita. Hanya ada satu, jadi **the**, seperti *the internet* dan *the government*. Tanpa artikel terdengar salah, dan *an environment* berarti salah satu dari banyak lingkungan (seperti *a work environment*, lingkungan kerja).

steps.title: each dan every
steps.text: Sekarang quantifier: kata yang menunjukkan berapa banyak. Pertama, each dan every.
steps.body:
Keduanya berarti *setiap* dan memakai kata benda serta kata kerja **tunggal**: *Every student **has** a laptop.* Bukan `every students`: pikirkan *setiap **satu** mahasiswa*.
- **every** = semua anggota kelompok (tiga atau lebih): *Every seat was taken.*
- **each** = satu per satu, masing-masing; juga untuk **dua**: *each side of the road*.
- Sebelum **of**, hanya each: *each of the rooms*. Bukan `every of` (bilang *every one of*).

Kelihatannya melanggar aturan: *every two weeks*. Dua minggu itu satu periode yang berulang.

pairs.id: setiap rekan kerja saya (satu per satu)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pak Hasan mengadakan pelatihan untuk karyawan baru bank.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ of the trainees gets a certificate at the end of the course.
question.explanation: Sebelum **of**, pakai **each**: *Each of the trainees gets …* dengan kata kerja tunggal (**gets**). `Every of` salah: harus *every one of*. *All of the trainees* butuh kata kerja jamak: *get*.

steps.title: both, either, neither, none
steps.text: Berikutnya: kata untuk dua hal, dan satu kata untuk tiga atau lebih.
steps.body:
Untuk **dua**:
- **both** = keduanya: *Both of my parents work.* (jamak)
- **either** = salah satu, yang mana saja: *You can take either bus.*
- **neither** = tidak dua-duanya: *Neither answer is right.*
Untuk **tiga atau lebih** (atau tak terhitung): **none of**: *None of my colleagues drives.*

**neither** dan **none** sudah negatif: `Neither of them didn't come` ✗.

Setelah *none of / neither of* + jamak, kata kerja tunggal atau jamak sama-sama boleh. Dan: *most people* (umum), *most of my friends* (tertentu).

pairs.id: tidak satu pun dari dua jawaban
tidak satu pun rekan kerja saya
tidak sepeser pun dari uang itu

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Rina dan suaminya diundang makan malam oleh rekan kerja, tapi malam itu mereka berdua sibuk.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kami berdua tidak bisa datang ke acara makan malam itu.
question.solution: Neither of us can come to the dinner.
question.explanation: **Neither of us** = kami berdua tidak. *neither* sudah negatif, jadi kata kerjanya tetap positif: **can come**, bukan *can't come*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas butuh uang tunai untuk ojek, jadi dia mencari ATM di dekat stasiun.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: He tried three ATMs, but ___ of them had any cash.
question.explanation: Tiga ATM itu lebih dari dua, jadi **none of**. *neither* hanya untuk dua, dan *both* untuk dua dan bermakna positif, jadi tidak cocok dengan *but … any*.
